bottom_line: In the main trial, mortality from any cause was similar with digoxin vs placebo (risk ratio when digoxin was compared with placebo, 0.99; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.91 to 1.07).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, digoxin vs placebo did not change all-cause mortality (0.99; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.91 to 1.07), while it was associated with fewer patients hospitalized for worsening heart failure (26.8 percent vs. 34.7 percent; risk ratio, 0.72; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.66 to 0.79) and more hospitalizations for suspected digoxin toxicity (2.0 vs. 0.9; risk ratio, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.42–3.32).

major_points.text: Primary outcome (mortality) showed no significant difference between groups.
major_points.quote: There were 1181 deaths (34.8 percent) with dig- oxin and 1194 deaths (35.1 percent) with placebo (risk ratio when digoxin was compared with placebo, 0.99; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.91 to 1.07; P  0.80).

major_points.text: Hospitalization for worsening heart failure was reduced with digoxin vs placebo.
major_points.quote: fewer patients were hospitalized for worsening heart failure (26.8 percent vs. 34.7 percent; risk ratio, 0.72; 95 percent confi- dence interval, 0.66 to 0.79; P0.001).

major_points.text: Suspected digoxin toxicity hospitalizations were more frequent with digoxin than placebo.

absolute_effects.text: All-cause death: 1181 (34.8) with digoxin vs 1194 (35.1) with placebo.
Hospitalization for worsening heart failure: 910 (26.8) with digoxin vs 1180 (34.7) with placebo.
Suspected digoxin toxicity hospitalization: 67 (2.0) with digoxin vs 31 (0.9) with placebo.
Overall combined outcome (death or hospitalization due to worsening heart failure): 1041/3397 (30.6) with digoxin vs 1291/3403 (37.9) with placebo.

subgroups.text: Subgroup results for the combined outcome (death or hospitalization due to worsening heart failure) are presented by EF strata.
Subgroup results for the combined outcome are presented by NYHA class (I/II vs III/IV).

harms.text: Suspected digoxin toxicity occurred more often with digoxin than placebo.
harms.quote: More patients had suspected digoxin toxicity in the digoxin group than in the placebo group (11.9 percent vs. 7.9 percent).

harms.text: Hospitalization for suspected digoxin toxicity was more frequent with digoxin than placebo.

inclusion_criteria.text: Ancillary trial enrolled heart failure patients with left ventricular ejection fraction greater than 0.45.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients with heart fail- ure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of more than 0.45 (988 patients) were enrolled in an ancillary trial conducted parallel to the main study.

analysis_methods.text: Analyses were performed on an intention-to-treat basis with two-sided P values.
analysis_methods.quote: All the analyses were performed on an intention-to-treat basis with two-sided P values.

analysis_methods.text: A stratified log-rank statistic compared survival distributions.
analysis_methods.quote: A stratified log-rank statistic was used to compare the survival distributions in the two study groups.
Kap- lan–Meier analysis was used to construct life-table plots.

analysis_methods.text: Risk ratios and 95% confidence intervals were estimated using the Cox proportional-hazards model.
analysis_methods.quote: calculated the 95 percent confidence interval from the Cox proportional-hazards model.

analysis_methods.text: Wilcoxon rank-sum test assessed between-group differences in number of hospitalizations.
analysis_methods.quote: The Wilcoxon rank-sum test was used to determine any differenc- es between groups in the number of hospitalizations.

trial_conduct.quote: An independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board monitored the progress of the study.

criticisms.text: Vital status was unknown for a small proportion of participants in the main trial.
criticisms.quote: the vital status of 47 patients assigned to digoxin and 46 patients assigned to placebo in the main trial (1.4 percent of the total) re- mains unknown.

criticisms.text: Death from other cardiac causes was not prespecified as a study outcome.
criticisms.quote: Although this outcome was not prespecified, P  0.04 for the comparison of study groups with respect to death from other cardiac causes.
